question.text: A loan of Rs. 10,00,000 at 7% p.a. (monthly rest) for 10 years has an EMI of Rs. 11,610. In the first EMI, the principal repaid is Rs. 5,777. The interest component of the first EMI is:

explanation.text: The Logic: First-month interest = Outstanding Principal x Monthly Rate = Rs. 10,00,000 x (7%/12) = Rs. 10,00,000 x 0.005833 = Rs. 5,833. Principal repaid = EMI - Interest = 11,610 - 5,833 = Rs. 5,777, which matches the given figure. The Trap: Rs. 7,000 is not the monthly interest component; it does not correspond to any clean step in the EMI breakup at 7% per annum on Rs. 10,00,000. Note: In the early months of an EMI schedule the interest component is the largest part of the EMI; it gradually declines as the outstanding principal reduces.
